message_2:
From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Pilot acceptance criteria — Clearview / Redwood

Emily — thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. Draft attached: Clearview_MAP_v1.xlsx. Key pieces included:

1) Success conditions (must pass all three to consider pilot a success):
   - Functional: end-to-end integration with Clearview EHR ingest and response mapping (sample mapping test suite).
   - Quality: 95% of sampled clinical prompts meet configured correctness thresholds (we provide sampling and scoring harness).
   - Performance: p95 latency <= 450ms for 512-token inference on dedicated pool; sustained throughput >= 8 requests/sec during 10-minute ramp.

2) Exit gates (any one triggers review / potential pause):
   - If p95 > 800ms for two consecutive full-day windows.
   - If false-positive rate on safety filters exceeds 2% for one rolling week.
   - If any data residency or audit log cannot be produced on request within 48 hours.

3) Acceptance tests (what Clearview runs, and what Redwood will provide):
   - Smoke scripts: connectivity, token exchange, end-to-end sig verification (we included acceptance-smoking-scripts.md).
   - Quality sampling: 200 random prompts from your clinical corpus (anonymized) scored via rubric (attached).
   - Load window: 10m ramp, 30m sustained at target throughput; monitoring dashboard with token-level breakdown.

4) Break-glass / fallback plan:
   - Immediate fallback to read-only mode (no model writes) with an SLA for rollback within 15 minutes of detection.
   - Canary to smaller model variant or region routing if throughput constraints appear.

Next steps I propose:
- You and procurement review the MAP and mark any blockers.
- We run a joint kickoff test (30–45 minutes) on 12/18 to validate connectivity and run the smoke scripts.

I've copied Marissa for acceptance test ownership and Ben for SLA/ops notes. Happy to hop on a 20-min sync if you want to walk through line-by-line.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Clearview_MAP_v1.xlsx

Looping in notes after a quick review of the draft MAP. High-level edits I want included before we share as final with Clearview:

- Quality thresholds: change wording from "95% of sampled clinical prompts" to "95% agreement with human rater on clinical correctness on blinded sample (n=200)" — avoids metric ambiguity.
- Performance tolerance windows: add a remediation bucket: if p95 is between 450ms and 650ms for a 24h window, trigger an ops review and one remediation sprint (not immediate exit). Only >800ms becomes a hard gate.
- Evidence artifacts: enumerate required logs (request_id, timestamp, model_variant, kv-cache-warm flag) and format (JSONL) — procurement insists on this.
- Compliance sign-off: add a short sign-off sheet our CS partner can sign at acceptance (we'll provide a template).

Also: Ben, please add an explicit note about who on ops will be on-call during the trial and the expected response time for incidents that meet break-glass (I recommend 15m for P0 degraded performance).

Connor — if you want, I can patch the spreadsheet and re-upload. We should get this to Emily before the 12/18 smoke run.

Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
message_4:

Cc: procure@clearviewhealth.com, laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Connor / Marissa — thanks for turning this around. Procurement reviewed the document and the edits look reasonable. A few clarifications from our side before we mark as mutual:

- Clinical correctness rubric: procurement wants to ensure rubric scoring will be blind and two-headed (two raters per sample) — we accept your n=200 but want inter-rater agreement >= 0.85.
- Reporting cadence: weekly automated CSV + dashboard link during the pilot; final report within 5 business days of pilot close.
- Stop condition language: procurement is comfortable with the remediation bucket as long as Redwood commits to a documented remediation plan within 48 hours of ops review.

We ran the smoke scripts on 12/18 (connectivity and a short load) — everything passed except one alert where p95 spiked to 520ms for a 6-minute window during the ramp; Redwood ops handled the failover and latency recovered. Can you add that event into the MAP incident log with root-cause and mitigation summary for our audit?

If you can add the edits and the incident log entry, we can route the MAP to legal and procurement for redlines and proceed with the test window on 01/04/2027.

Emily Santos
Director, Vendor Integrations
Clearview Health

Attachments referenced: acceptance-smoking-scripts.md (from Redwood), Clearview feedback summary (procurement-comments.pdf)
